normalized.description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design a satellite system for FRMCS which is operating in the same frequency bands as the terrestrial counterpart (i.e., 900 MHz and 1.9 GHz), with the purpose to exclusively service the coverage gaps of the terrestrial network while avoiding interference. The performance of such system will be evaluated with the development of a system simulator.Targeted Improvements: - Reduce by 80% the cost of the satellite system for FRMCS.- Reduce by 50% the cost of on-board railway terminals, by allowing a single terminal solution for terrestrial and satellite FRMCS connectivity.Description: The Future RailwayMobile Communication System (FRMCS), being a successor of the GSM-R system, is planned to be operational before GSM-R's predicted saturation in 2030. Through standardisation work, satcom is established as a component of the future system, while it is found that the satellite integration into FRMCS is simplified when satcom is employing the 5G NR, which is the selected air interface for the terrestrial FRMCS access. However, the frequency bands for such a service via satellite and the design of the satellite system are yetto be concluded. The advantages of an innovative approach, where the satellite offers connectivity exclusively to the coverage gapsofsuch terrestrial network, have been recently reported. In fact, such a satellite system targeting only the terrestrial coverage gaps while ignoring the areas serviced by theterrestrial network, will have a lower complexity and overall cost, as fewer satellites of less capacity will be required. In addition, such a satellite system will be able to operate in the same frequency bands as theterrestrial network (i.e., 900 MHz and 1.9 GHz), as each network (terrestrial or satellite) will not be available in the same area where the other network operates and therefore they will not interfere with each other. This usage of the same frequency from the satellite and the terrestrial network not only facilitates the integration of the two networks into FRMCS, but also potentially allow the usage of the same terminal for both networks, a solution that is very favourable for railway operators. This activity will thereforeinvestigate the design of a 5G NR based satellite system for FRMCS which exclusively targets the terrestrial network gaps of communication and operates in the same frequency bands as the terrestrial FRMCS network. The activity will include a traffic characterisation and capacity analysis for the terrestrial network gaps which will then feed the system design and the element sizing of the ground and space components. The impact of the railway-satellite channel for the 900 MHz and the 1900 GHz will also be thoroughly investigated. The best numerologies and 5G NR configurations will also be identified for such a satellite system. The work will be supported by the development of a system simulator which will investigate the FRMCS 5G NR satellite link performance and achieved C/I ratios under a variety of different orbits, system architectures, frequency bands, channel conditions and air interface configurations. The activity will also investigate and conclude on the feasibility of having a single modem and a single antenna equipped on board the trains, which offer connectivity both to the satellite and the terrestrial network at different time instances.

ESA/ESEC is the ESA European Space Security and Education Centre located in Belgium and is one of the ESA sites in Europe. The main core business in Mission Operations relevant to this procurement are:  Control dedicated Satellites and Ground Segment (so called "Small Satellite missions")  Perform its In-Orbit activities.  Host and operate some ground segment elements in support to the EU Space Programme within a secured environment - mainly Galileo and EGNOS The Operational services, within the scope specified above, will be therefore divided in two main WPs: WP-1 Small Satellites Operations:   A number of Small Satellites (such as the PROBA ones) are or will be controlled from ESEC with the help of a dedicated ground segment. In the current set-up and number of missions, up to six passes per satellite daily are supported in automatic mode for TM reception and commanding, which may be extended in the future when new missions will be operated from ESEC. The mission products are made available at ESEC and ready for distribution. The Small Satellites Mission Operations Centre is therefore responsible of the monitoring and control of the satellite and the corresponding ground segment, the handling of the user requests, the extraction of the mission products and their availability for distribution.  The Small Satellites operations concept relies on a highly automatic functioning of the ground segment and a high degree of autonomy in the space segment for the delayed execution of operations requested by telecommand and for satellite survival. No operator attended shift work is foreseen. Operational engineers supervise the small satellites mission operations and related performances usually only during normal working hours. Provisions for an On-Call service shall be also considered for the WP. Occasional working outside normal working hours and overtime may be required. The satellites are safe by design and can survive for a long period without ground station contact.   This WP will cover OPSPREP and OPS activities, support to Industry, execution of delegated tasks for critical operations (LEOP, others) together and in collaboration with Industry for this small satellite missions. This WP may implement further mission operations engineering activities carried out in support of other ESA programmes requested by ESA programme directorates to OPS. WP-2 Galileo Hosting activities:  The Galileo Hosting support will be provided in response to the requirements and agreements reached with EUSPA for Galileo and EGNOS. The provision of support to the hosting and testing activities will be performed on-site during normal working hours. Provisions for an On-Call service shall be also considered for the WP. Occasional working outside normal working hours and overtime may be required. The Agency will issue one single Invitation to Tender in Open Competition for the two WPs. Considering the relatively small volume covered by this procurement, the Tenderers will be invited to provide a single proposal covering the support to both areas.   The new contract is planned to be kicked-off starting in 1st Quarter 2027 (phase-in) as required to permit sufficient time for a smooth transition (e.g. training, certification of new service provider's personnel).  The operational phase of the contract is expected to start latest by 2nd Quarter 2027, at the expiry of the current INDUSTRIAL SERVICE PROVISION IN SUPPORT OF THE OPERATION OF ESA IN BELGIUM contract extension.

These types of carbon fibres providehigh strength/weight andhigh stiffness/weight ratio in composite structures, ensuring both mechanicalperformance and dimensional stability for composites.High performance composite materials are widelyused in ESA launch vehicles, as well as primary structures of spacecrafts (such as Sentinels or Galileo) or robotic exploration platforms. According to a market study, the demand for carbon fibres for polymercomposite materials for space applications in Europe between 2023 and 2032 is estimated at approximately450 t.High-performance carbon fibres qualified for space flight are currently sourced from outside Europe and/orlinked to non-EU IP and export regimes, representing a strategic dependency. There have been someprojects on the development of pilot lines for carbon fibre manufacturing, such as the EUCARBON (FP7)and Space Carbon (H2020) activities, but the developed manufacturing capabilities are still in their earlystages and without clear plans on industrialization and utilization of the products. There are some limitedmanufacturing plants in Europe, however most of them use precursors (raw materials) that are imported,which again leads to foreign dependence. There are currently no existing, readily available and qualifiedcarbon fibres with a fully sovereign supply chain in Europe.The activity will focus onthe mechanical characterization, processability and industrialization, and conformity with ESA qualification standards. Its objective is to strengthen the development of a robust and autonomous European supply chain. The scope of the work targets RD activities carried out with European companies striving to replicateor exceedthe performance of competing solutions originating from outside Europe.Therefore, the following, not exhaustive, tasks shall be executed:- Identification of a fully European supply chain (including precursors and prepregging) to be assessed for their material systems and processes compatibility with space applications. Preferably define a supply chain able to realize prepregs from HM fibers and a supply chain to realize HS fiber tow for filament winding.- A characterization of the identified material systems for space applications, both at fiber level and at laminatelevel. Laminate level characterization shall be performed on samples manufactured using processes thatare common in space industry. Preferably autoclave process of prepregs with high modulus fibers andfilament winding with high strength fiber system. Benchmark results against ESA-qualified, non-Europeanmaterial systems to identify performance gaps and qualification needs.- Manufacture breadboards of representative space structural components using the identified HM and HSmaterial systems and relative processes. In this phase of the project the involvement of already establishedEuropean space composite structures designers, manufacturers and test houses is highlyrecommended.- Develop a database based on the acquired results and provide recommendations for standardization, furtherdevelopment and potential qualification and industrialization paths including a preliminary budget and time estimate.- An overview of the steps needed towards industrialization of a product of high-quality, assessment of facilities wrt re-use/adapt vs build dedicated one, long-term commercial viability plan (including discussions with the end users, lessons learned from other industries or other countries should be incorporated in this plan, for example ways to reduce the energy needed in a production planned).

normalized.description: Objective: The activity objective is to design, manufacturing and test a high-performance programmable reference oscillator basedon microelectromechanical (MEMS) resonator operating in the 10 - 500 MHz range to serve as a reference oscillator or to attend directly as local oscillator the lower frequency range for telecom application.Targeted Improvements: - Enabling a European or Canadian source of a MEMS oscillator chip suitable for system on chip (SoC) integration.- Size, weight and power reduction by several orders of magnitude versus current technology of quartz OCXO.- Increase of fractional-N frequency generation by a factor of more than5.Description:Current telecom satellite payload equipment used mainly quartz-based oscillators for clock generation reference signals, used for track-and-hold amplifiers and digital-to-analogue (DAC) and analogue-to-digital (ADC) blocks in direct conversion (zero-IF or homodyne) frequency converters; for I-Q demodulator blocks in fully digital beamforming networks; and in double conversion super heterodyne frequency converters local oscillators (LOs) at different carrier frequencies. However, European sources of quartz-based oscillatorsare becoming more limited, and these solutions are expensive, with a form factor and power consumption that becomes challenging when incorporating into highly integrated payloads. Current state-of-art oscillators based on microelectromechanical(MEMS) resonators display competitive phase noise and frequency stability performance compared to quartz-based solutions, but thereare no European or Canadian sources of such products. Important advantages of such MEMS resonators compared to quartz-based oscillatorcan be seen, where MEMS achieves performance in between the Temperature Controlled Crystal Oscillator (TCXO) and Oven ControlledCrystal Oscillators (OCXOs) but with the advantage of their extremely small form factor, low power consumption and integration capability with Silicon process. One more important aspect is that the MEMS fundamentalmode frequency can be much higher than that of aQuartz crystal, whereas cost reduction is expected at lower frequencies and better performance at higher frequencies.This activity will design, manufacture of an engineering model oscillator chip based on European microelectromechanical technology in the 10 and500 MHz frequency range. The performance shall be suitable for a range of application scenarios in telecom payloads. The engineering model chip shall be built and tested in a critical environment, including thermal test

originalText: {"job":"institution-ESA-issued-competition","collectionState":"reconciled","verifiedOpen":false,"spaceRelevance":"not_assessed","recordType":"discovery_candidate","evidence":{"file":"institution-ESA-issued-competition/page-2-1aafdf39419199804722d3e64e73c7277a2166c54d4dd460c81c8b4426ed2914.json","sha256":"1aafdf39419199804722d3e64e73c7277a2166c54d4dd460c81c8b4426ed2914","row":5,"retrievedAt":"2026-10-21T08:21:52.140Z"},"original":{"activityNumber":"1000045730","closingDate":"2026-11-18T13:00:00","clarificationRequestDeadline":"2026-11-11T13:00:00","description":"Objective: To model the hypersonic flow around critical points of the re-entry of a upper stage vehicle, accounting for the catalytic properties of a Si-O-C ceramics, and for the chemical modifications of the surface exposed to the air.Description: There is a renewed interest in the implementation of reusable vehicles for in-orbit operation. A critical aspect in the lifetime of a space vehicle is to improve the durability of the thermal protection structures, to limit the replacement of the thermal shield. Ultra-high temperature ceramics (UHTC) materials, based on the Si-O-C compounds with dedicated coatings (boride, molybdenum etc.) demonstrated to be a good choice, due to their capability to resist and survive above 1500 K. To fully evaluate the response of any material in suchextreme operating conditions, it is also imperative to determine the catalysis in high temperature gas, strongly affecting the surface heat flux. Moreover, the interaction of the material coatings with dissociated gases such as oxygen and nitrogen, induces variations on the material properties. This activity aims at developing a comprehensive set of tools (e.g. DRAMA like tool, prototype software for formation flying) that ensure monitoring, risk assessment, and collision avoidance during close proximity operations (including formation flying).
